proposed_from.topic: PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: At one fixed smooth boundary point b, observe iid units from a uniform two-sided half-disc with Bernoulli outcomes whose side means lie in [1/4,3/4] and are L-Lipschitz, but retain only treatment side and radial point-distance Q_Delta(R)=Delta floor(R/Delta), not angle or raw coordinates. Target tau(b). Prove minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order max{n^(-1/4),Delta}, with squared risk of the corresponding squared order, uniformly across Delta, using a bin-aware local estimator with explicit Lipschitz bias. The lower seed is exact: on the treated first bin set phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u), u=R/Delta; half-disc radial density is proportional to u and integral_0^1 u phi(u)du=0, so a Bernoulli-mean perturbation c Delta phi gives the same rounded-bin law while changing the boundary limit by c Delta and retaining bounded derivative. The rd2d.distance R, Python, and Stata workflow and its Ser Pilo Paga replication are the consumer. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a same-class lower combining sampling and aliasing rather than merely maximizing separate bounds, construct total honest intervals for all Delta regimes, and state exactly what coordinate coarsening the analyst observes. EARLY KILL TEST: Drop if Dong-Kolesar or discrete-running-variable RD already yields this 2D radial-compression point-BATEC frontier, if the weighted integral identity or Bernoulli-mixture equality fails, or if raw coordinates remain available.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, Theorem 4, Section 6, Theorem 6, and Conclusion
seed_details.summary: Prove absolute and squared minimax risk of orders \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) and \(\max\{n^{-1/2},\Delta^2\}\) by one bin-aware upper bound and one same-class pair combining a local sampling bump with an invisible first-bin alias.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact-radius testing likelihoods by grouped Bernoulli cell means and superpose a zero-cell-mean perturbation without spending additional testing distance.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for rounded boundary discontinuity distance, quantized radius regression discontinuity, and rounded BATEC found no matching target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance plus a separate rounding lower bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: The exact-radius paper does not define the grouped experiment, and separate witnesses do not certify one transition-uniform pair under a shared Bernoulli range and Lipschitz budget.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, Section 5, Proposition 1, proof in Appendix A.5, and Conclusion
seed_details.summary: Construct an everywhere-defined exact-binomial interval with explicit radial Lipschitz bias and prove minimax honest expected length of order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace fixed support-point local-linear weights by known half-disc bin probabilities of order \(H^2\), then control zero-count samples without conditioning on an invertible Gram matrix.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for honest intervals with rounded running variables and radial bins found only ordinary discrete-RD and exact-distance BDD inference.
seed_details.red_team: KolesarRothe2018Discrete already gives honest confidence intervals for discrete running variables.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its interval does not treat a latent continuously distributed radius, annular averaging bias, quadratic local mass, or totality when the radial local design is empty.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction and the point-location identification discussion around the boundary treatment-effect curve
seed_details.summary: Order the minimax experiments generated by raw coordinates, exact radius, side plus rounded radius, rounded Cartesian coordinates, and radius plus angle, and characterize which retained coordinates remove the order-\(\Delta\) alias.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Factor each likelihood through its observation \(\sigma\)-field and identify whether within-annulus position is measurable.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining boundary treatment effects with rounded coordinates or quantized distance returned no experiment-comparison theorem.
seed_details.red_team: The ordering follows mechanically from data processing.
seed_details.rebuttal: Data processing gives only weak ordering; rate equivalences and necessity of specific retained coordinates require distinct legal lower witnesses and matching procedures.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Identification proof via shrinking level-set integrals, smooth-boundary bias theorem, and Conclusion
seed_details.summary: Give necessary and sufficient local radial-weight conditions for an order-\(\Delta\) alias under curved boundaries and unknown nonuniform design density, with a matching grouped estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the exact weight \(u\) by the tubular-coordinate Jacobian and solve a uniformly Lipschitz weighted moment-zero problem using only released counts.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found measurement-error corrections requiring an error law, but no density-free rounded-annulus alias criterion.
seed_details.red_team: A weighted orthogonal polynomial makes the extension routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The weight is latent when coordinates are suppressed, so both existence of a uniform null direction and implementable upper calibration become identification questions.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, Theorem 1, Corollary 1, proof by iterated expectations and moment-matrix inversion, and Section 10
seed_details.summary: Compare deterministic floor rounding with a released public random dither and derive whether dither removes the alias floor or merely changes its constant.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition the latent radial integral jointly on the released dither and bin rather than on one deterministic cell.
seed_details.destination_search: Dithered quantization appears in signal-processing regression, but the search found no causal RD boundary target or radial Lipschitz frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Known dither trivially reconstructs the raw radius.
seed_details.rebuttal: Subtractive dither does not reconstruct within-cell position from a single quantized measurement; whether its randomized cells destroy a fixed null direction is a nontrivial experiment question.

seed_details.summary: Characterize when two offset rounded radii eliminate the first-bin nullspace and restore the exact-radius rate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Intersect the two annular averaging kernels and determine injectivity on the Lipschitz tangent cone.
seed_details.destination_search: Targeted searches for multiple rounded running-variable measurements in boundary RD found no theorem for offset radial grids.
seed_details.red_team: Two grids simply create a finer grid with width equal to their greatest common divisor.
seed_details.rebuttal: That conclusion depends on commensurability and joint release; irrational or stochastic offsets generate a different inverse problem whose stability, not only injectivity, determines the rate.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 4 pointwise convergence rate and Supplemental Appendix pointwise normal approximation
seed_details.summary: For \(\Delta=\kappa n^{-1/4}\), derive the local asymptotic experiment and the limit law of an optimally calibrated grouped estimator as a function of \(\kappa\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace continuous kernel-score linearization by a triangular multinomial array whose first few annuli retain nonvanishing discretization geometry after rescaling.
seed_details.destination_search: No transition limit law for floor-rounded radial BDD data appeared in searches of exact-distance, discrete-RD, or measurement-error RD work.
seed_details.red_team: A central limit theorem follows directly because the estimator is a sum of Bernoulli variables.
seed_details.rebuttal: Normality of a fixed estimator is routine, but the \(\kappa\)-indexed local experiment, bias drift, and optimal calibration across changing bin geometry are not.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, ordered-modulus construction, regression-discontinuity specialization, and expected-length efficiency bounds
seed_details.summary: Evaluate the rounded radial modulus in the Gaussian limit experiment and derive the sharp local asymptotic minimax and honest-length constants for each fixed transition ratio \(\kappa=\Delta n^{1/4}\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Solve the convex modulus after replacing point evaluations by radial bin-average operators with weights proportional to \(r\).
seed_details.destination_search: Armstrong--Koles\'ar treat general linear functionals and ordinary RD, but the search found no evaluated modulus for radial floor bins.
seed_details.red_team: This is a direct numerical application of the general modulus theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The theorem is general, but analytic characterization of the least-favorable Lipschitz pair and its \(\kappa\)-dependent constant is the substantive unsolved operator problem.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Corollary 1 and the unknown-rounding-moment bounds following Equation 5
seed_details.summary: Derive closed-form sharp endpoints for \(m_t(0)\) from all population annular means under the Lipschitz bound, then attach uniform plug-in inference.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace finite-dimensional polynomial moment inversion by a Lipschitz extension problem from weighted annular averages to the boundary value.
seed_details.destination_search: The scan found abstract smoothness bounds for discrete RD but no closed-form radial-Jacobian endpoint map.
seed_details.red_team: The first bin alone gives the trivial interval \(\bar m_{t,0}\pm O(\Delta)\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Sharp constants and compatibility across all bins require solving a global Lipschitz moment problem, although its consumer value is lower than the joint finite-sample frontier.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 4 pointwise rate and Theorem 5 inference
seed_details.summary: Seek a regular semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau_P(b)\) in the rounded-radius Lipschitz model.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Attempt pathwise differentiation through the grouped observation operator.
seed_details.destination_search: The fixed-point Lipschitz target is nonregular even before quantization, obstructing a classical influence-function bound.
seed_details.red_team: The target is not pathwise differentiable, so a regular semiparametric efficiency bound is the wrong object.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; the credible efficiency lane is the nonregular modulus constant in \(\mathrm{seed:sharp\text{-}modulus\text{-}constant}\), so this seed is dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A classical M11(b) framing would force regular influence-function language onto a nonregular point-evaluation problem.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Supplemental Appendix discussion of weighted and largest boundary effects
seed_details.summary: Choose a treatment policy from rounded radial data and derive welfare regret.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace fixed-point estimation loss by an empirical welfare objective.
seed_details.destination_search: No natural policy class is specified by the fixed-boundary, deterministic-assignment substrate.
seed_details.red_team: This changes the scientific target from estimating a fixed BATEC value to choosing treatment, so it is not an adjacent unresolved theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; the M16 lane is dropped rather than relabeling estimation error as regret.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: M16 requires a treatment-choice rule and welfare oracle, neither of which is present in the named opportunity.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction and Section 5 honest confidence intervals
seed_details.summary: Invert a permutation or conformal statistic to obtain finite-sample coverage for the rounded-radius boundary effect.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Search for an exchangeability group preserving the sharp RD counterfactual null.
seed_details.destination_search: The deterministic side assignment and observational potential outcomes supply no randomization group or exchangeable missing-counterfactual orbit.
seed_details.red_team: Permuting outcomes across sides is invalid because treatment is deterministic and the radial regressions may differ.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; exact marginal binomial inversion is available, but it is not an M17 symmetry argument, so this seed is dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Calling exact binomial inversion conformal would confuse a parametric tail inversion with symmetry-based counterfactual coverage.
